subject.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings

question: Which Feishu bind grammar should OpenClaw accept before adopting any candidate fix for conversation-level Feishu routing?
rationale: The central bug is real, but the PR changes a documented CLI grammar and persisted binding shape; automation cannot safely choose whether to preserve `feishu:<account>`, add explicit peer syntax, or use a Feishu/plugin-owned recognizer.

options.title: Preserve account grammar and add peer syntax
options.body: Keep `<channel>:<account>` unchanged and add an explicit conversation/peer form or plugin-owned recognizer with docs and upgrade proof.

options.title: Adopt a Feishu prefix recognizer
options.body: Use Feishu conversation-id prefixes such as group/user ids to infer peers while leaving unknown values as account IDs.

options.title: Intentionally reinterpret `feishu:<id>`
options.body: Accept this PR's default group-peer interpretation only with maintainer-approved docs, migration guidance, and proof that existing account binds are not a supported concern.

recommendation.title: Preserve account grammar and add peer syntax
recommendation.body: Keep `<channel>:<account>` unchanged and add an explicit conversation/peer form or plugin-owned recognizer with docs and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent docs/routing history makes this the best available owner for the public CLI grammar and route-binding semantics decision.
